boundary_singularity_theorem.approach: s=epsilon-i*t with epsilon down to zero
boundary_singularity_theorem.boundary_subtraction_poles: -1/(exp(pi*s)-1) has simple poles at s=2*i*q, equivalently t in 2*Z
boundary_singularity_theorem.overlap_boundary: axis branch locations can coincide with boundary-subtraction poles, but their singularity types differ and no cancellation is asserted
boundary_singularity_theorem.singularity_type: boundary branch singularity of power -3/2; no isolated-orbit amplitude is inferred

formal_lift.operator: sqrt(Delta_D) for the unit-square Dirichlet Laplacian

geometric_decomposition.multiplicity_rule: four sign lifts are already absorbed into coefficient 2*s/pi; ordered positive coordinate swaps remain separate

numerical_method.complex_remainder_bound: after two terms, each summand is at most 15*|s|^4/(8*3^(7/2)*|m|^7) for |m|>=M>=|s|
numerical_method.square_shell_bound: maxnorm shell k has 8*k points and sum_(k>M) k^(-6)<=1/(5*M^5)

poisson_theorem.absolute_convergence: both the primal trace and the dual |m|^(-3) series converge absolutely and locally uniformly on Re(s)>0
poisson_theorem.branch: principal power, holomorphic because s^2+4|m|^2 avoids the nonpositive real axis for Re(s)>0
poisson_theorem.proof_route: Poisson summation for real s>0 by Gaussian regularization, followed by half-plane analytic continuation

source_lock.clock: Dirichlet half-wave time, approached by s=epsilon-i*t
source_lock.forbidden_data: target tables, prime tables, arithmetic local or Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, Hilbert--Polya, Route B
source_lock.object: Dirichlet Laplacian on the unit square
source_lock.ordered_direction_convention: a,b>=1 with gcd(a,b)=1; coordinate swaps remain distinct
source_lock.precision: exact integer shell arithmetic and 55-decimal mpmath sentinels with explicit tail bounds
